gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its profits every year since it changed strategy, and analysts expect more growth.
gaps.hint: since clause anchors past to present
gaps.explanation: A 'since' clause connecting a past start to the present requires the present perfect: has increased.

gaps.sentence: She ___ two majors when she was at university.
gaps.hint: a completed period in the past
gaps.explanation: A completed past period takes the past simple: did.

gaps.sentence: Look at those clouds — it ___ any minute now.
gaps.explanation: A prediction based on present evidence uses 'be going to': is going to rain.

gaps.sentence: Her eyes were red because she ___.
gaps.hint: visible result of an earlier activity
gaps.explanation: The past perfect continuous shows an activity whose results were visible at a past moment: had been crying.

gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: Wait there and I ___ you some aspirin.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous offer at the moment
gaps.explanation: Offers made spontaneously at the moment of speaking use 'will': will get.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.
